key.name: model
key.summary: LLM model override
key.description: The Ollama model identifier for LLM inference. Empty means auto-select based on hardware capabilities; set explicitly to override.

key.name: vision-model
key.summary: Vision model override
key.description: The Ollama model identifier the vision sense describes screen and camera captures with. Empty means auto-select by hardware tier. Deliberately independent of "model" and of the --model command line flag: that setting is about chat, a text model has no vision tower, and changing one must not silently change the other. Must name a LOCAL Ollama model - a URL, a host, or any other remote reference is refused rather than sent a screenshot.

key.name: hardware-profile
key.summary: Hardware profile for model selection
key.description: Selects the model, whisper, and context-window tier based on hardware. Supported values: "auto" (detect at startup), "low", "medium", "high", "gpu". Applied during component initialization at startup; an unknown or blank value behaves like "auto".

key.name: privacy-mode
key.summary: Enable privacy-first local-only mode
key.description: When true, all processing happens locally. No data is sent to external servers.

key.name: whisper-model
key.summary: Whisper.cpp model override
key.description: The whisper.cpp model to use for transcription. Empty means auto-select based on hardware capabilities; set explicitly (e.g. "tiny", "base", "medium") to override.

key.name: piper-voice
key.summary: Piper TTS voice to use
key.description: The voice model for text-to-speech synthesis.

key.name: ollama-host
key.summary: Ollama server host URL
key.description: The URL of the Ollama inference server.

key.name: auto-start
key.summary: Auto-start on login
key.description: Whether to automatically start shani-chronoa on user login.

key.name: notification-enabled
key.summary: Enable spoken replies and timer notifications
key.description: When true, Chronoa speaks its replies aloud (text-to-speech) and timer completions fire a desktop notification. When false, replies are shown on screen only and timers stay silent.

key.name: language
key.summary: Interface and processing language
key.description: The language code for speech recognition and interface text.

key.name: debug-mode
key.summary: Enable debug logging
key.description: When true, verbose debug output is logged for troubleshooting.

key.name: wake-word-enabled
key.summary: Enable hands-free wake-word activation
key.description: When true and openWakeWord is installed, listens continuously for the wake word instead of requiring a button press.

key.name: wake-word-model
key.summary: Wake-word model to listen for
key.description: The openWakeWord pretrained model name to activate on. No dedicated "hey chronoa" model has been trained yet, so this defaults to one of openWakeWord's bundled phrases.

key.name: cloud-fallback-enabled
key.summary: Allow falling back to a free cloud LLM when Ollama is unavailable
key.description: When true AND privacy mode is off, Chronoa may send prompts to a free, no-API-key cloud LLM gateway (LLM7, Kilo Gateway, or BlockRun) if Ollama cannot be reached. Off by default - this is the one setting that sends data off the machine.

key.name: barge-in-vad-enabled
key.summary: Interrupt spoken replies as soon as you start talking
key.description: When true, continuously monitors the microphone while Chronoa is speaking and interrupts immediately on detected speech, instead of only interrupting on the next button press or wake word. Off by default: there is no acoustic echo cancellation, so on speakers (not headphones) the mic may pick up Chronoa's own voice and self-interrupt.

key.name: audio-input-device
key.summary: PipeWire node name to record from
key.description: Empty means whatever PipeWire treats as the default microphone. Otherwise this must be a PipeWire node name as listed by `shani-chronoa-sense devices` or by `pw-cli ls Node`, and it is applied as `pw-record --target`. Only honoured on the PipeWire backends: ALSA's arecord takes a different identifier (hw:0,0), not a PipeWire node name.

key.name: audio-output-device
key.summary: PipeWire node name to play through
key.description: Empty means whatever PipeWire treats as the default output. Otherwise this must be a PipeWire node name, applied as `pw-play --target`. Only honoured on the PipeWire backends: ALSA's aplay takes a different identifier, not a PipeWire node name.

key.name: llm7-api-key
key.summary: Optional LLM7 API key (BYOK)
key.description: Bring-your-own-key for the LLM7 free cloud gateway. Empty uses anonymous access (no key required); a real key may raise rate limits.

key.name: kilo-api-key
key.summary: Optional Kilo Gateway API key (BYOK)
key.description: Bring-your-own-key for the Kilo Gateway free cloud gateway. Empty uses anonymous access; Kilo's own rate-limit errors suggest a real key raises the limit.

key.name: blockrun-api-key
key.summary: Optional BlockRun API key (BYOK)
key.description: Bring-your-own-key for the BlockRun free cloud gateway. Empty uses anonymous access, which shares a global free-tier quota with every other anonymous user.

key.name: openai-api-key
key.summary: OpenAI API key
key.description: Required to use OpenAI as a cloud LLM fallback - OpenAI has no anonymous access. Empty means this provider is skipped.

key.name: anthropic-api-key
key.summary: Anthropic API key
key.description: Required to use Anthropic (Claude) as a cloud LLM fallback - Anthropic has no anonymous access. Empty means this provider is skipped.

key.name: google-api-key
key.summary: Google Gemini API key
key.description: Required to use Google Gemini as a cloud LLM fallback - Google has no anonymous access. Empty means this provider is skipped.

key.name: groq-api-key
key.summary: Groq API key
key.description: Required to use Groq as a cloud LLM fallback - Groq has no anonymous access. Empty means this provider is skipped.

key.name: vision-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa see the screen
key.description: When true, Chronoa may capture and describe what is on screen. Off by default: this is the widest privacy surface Chronoa has. Also requires privacy mode to be off for any cloud processing. Reactive only - Chronoa looks when you ask it to, it does not watch continuously.

key.name: ocr-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read text from images
key.description: When true, Chronoa may extract text from images and screenshots you point it at, using local tesseract. Off by default. Processing is entirely local.

key.name: filesystem-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read files
key.description: When true, Chronoa may read files inside your home directory that you name. Off by default. Reads are confined to your home directory and size-capped; nothing outside it is reachable.

key.name: web-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa retrieve web content
key.description: When true, Chronoa may fetch web pages and read their contents. Off by default. This is the one sense that sends a request off the machine, so it also requires privacy mode to be off.

key.name: smart-sense-enabled
key.summary: Retired: merged into the storage sense
key.description: The `smart` sense was merged into `storage` - both describe the same physical drives, and `storage` was already reporting NVMe wear from sysfs while `smart` read the same endurance figure from SMART attribute 233. One walk of /sys/block now reports identity, capacity, wear and SMART health together. This key is still honoured: setting it to true grants the `storage` sense, so a grant made before the merge is not revoked by it.

key.name: gpu-sense-enabled
key.summary: Graphics
key.description: When true, Chronoa may read which gpu this machine has, its driver, and how much video memory. On by default because it reads the machine, not you, and never leaves it. Anything needing a tool that is not installed reports that it was not determined rather than a clean negative.

key.name: cooling-sense-enabled
key.summary: Retired: merged into the hwmon sense
key.description: The `cooling` sense was merged into `hwmon`, which reported fan speeds and liquid coolers. The kernel exposes the same sensors through both the thermal-zone and the hwmon trees and they agree, so one sense now reports chips, fans, liquid cooling and thermal zones together. This key is still honoured: setting it to true grants the `hwmon` sense, so a grant made before the merge is not revoked by it.

key.name: security-sense-enabled
key.summary: Firmware security
key.description: When true, Chronoa may read secure boot, tpm presence, lockdown mode and the security modules in effect. On by default because it reads the machine, not you, and never leaves it. Reports a check it could not run as undetermined rather than as passing, and never ranks settings it has not verified are in effect.

key.name: devices-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa inventory the hardware buses
key.description: When true, Chronoa may list what is on the PCI and USB buses: each device with its class, vendor and device id, the driver bound to it, and for USB the port it is in and its link speed. On by default because it reads the machine, not you, and never leaves it. Flags a PCI device with no driver bound, which is hardware the kernel does not know what to do with, and separates USB root hubs from peripherals.

key.name: audio-sense-enabled
key.summary: Audio devices
key.description: When true, Chronoa may read what the machine can play and record, and at what volume. On by default because it reads the machine, not you, and never leaves it. Anything needing a tool that is not installed reports that it was not determined rather than a clean negative.

key.name: monitors-sense-enabled
key.summary: Retired: merged into the display sense
key.description: The `monitors` sense was merged into `display` - both walked /sys/class/drm and both reported which connectors were connected, so one enumeration now reports the backlight and the panel identity together. This key is still honoured: setting it to true grants the `display` sense, so a permission granted before the merge is not revoked by it. It will be removed in a future release once no supported install can still hold it.

key.name: capture-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read the capture devices and who is holding them
key.description: When true, Chronoa may read which capture devices this machine has - cameras and microphones - and which process currently holds each one open. Off by default because this names the applications you are running at this moment, which is about you rather than about the machine. A device that cannot be checked is reported as undetermined and never as free: a missing holder-lookup tool and a genuinely idle camera look identical from here, and only one of them means nobody is watching.

key.name: printing-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read which printers and scanners this machine has
key.description: When true, Chronoa may read which printers are configured in CUPS, which is the default destination, and which scanners the SANE backends detect. Off by default because a printer and scanner inventory describes the physical peripherals someone has chosen to connect, which is a step further than reading the machine's own specifications. It never prints or scans anything - only the two inventories are read - so enabling it has no physical effect. A missing cups or sane package is reported as the missing package it is, not as an absence of printers or scanners.

key.name: cpu-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read processor and load state
key.description: When true, Chronoa may read how many CPUs are online, the load average and how many tasks are runnable, available memory and swap, uptime, and the frequency governor. On by default because it reads the machine, not you, and never leaves it. Load is reported per CPU rather than as a percentage, because load counts runnable tasks and not CPU time.

key.name: link-sense-enabled
key.summary: Retired: merged into the network sense
key.description: The `link` sense was merged into `network` - both walked /sys/class/net and both printed the same per-interface state line, with `link` adding the negotiated speed and `network` adding the wireless flag and DNS. One enumeration now reports interface state, link speed, wireless, DNS and whether this is a bridge or container network. This key is still honoured: setting it to true grants the `network` sense, so an install that allowed `link` before the merge keeps that permission. Its default is false, deliberately: `link` used to default to true, and a retired key that defaults to true would silently override `network-sense-enabled`, making the switch in the settings window appear to do nothing. The default-on behaviour now lives on `network-sense-enabled`, which is the one a user actually sees.

key.name: storage-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read disk inventory
key.description: When true, Chronoa may read which physical disks this machine has, their capacity, and for NVMe drives how much write endurance is used. On by default because it reads the machine, not you, and never leaves it. This is disk inventory, not health: SMART health needs a tool from an opt-in package and root on most drives, so Chronoa reports health as undetermined rather than guessing.

key.name: power-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read battery and power state
key.description: When true, Chronoa may read your battery charge, wear and cycle count, and whether a mains adapter is online. On by default because it reads the machine, not you: it is the same class of fact as a disk-free reading, and it never leaves the machine. Switch it off to stop even that being polled.

key.name: memory-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa remember things between sessions
key.description: When true, Chronoa keeps durable notes about you across sessions so it does not have to be re-told the same things. On by default because remembering is what makes an assistant useful over time. Everything stays on this machine; you can erase it at any time from the settings window or the shani-chronoa-sense CLI.

key.name: hearing-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa hear what you say
key.description: When true, an utterance you speak may be turned into a transient percept so the assistant can refer to it in the turn. Off by default: microphone capture is the widest privacy surface Chronoa has, alongside vision. Utterances are transient and are never durable - only the memory sense may persist. This is the consent gate for the sense; it does not control wake-word listening or TTS.

key.name: contention-sense-enabled
key.summary: Retired: merged into the capture sense
key.description: The `contention` sense was merged into `capture`. They already shared the device-holder lookup - `camera` imported `contention.describe` - and `contention` already walked both the video and the sound nodes, so one sense now reports every capture device, what the kernel calls it, and whether anything holds it open. This key is still honoured: setting it to true grants the `capture` sense, so a grant made before the merge is not revoked by it.

key.name: privilege-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa report which programs hold elevated Linux capabilities
key.description: When true, Chronoa may read each process's effective capability set from /proc and report those holding a capability that can sniff network traffic, load kernel modules, or override ownership checks. Off by default. Read-only and vendor-neutral: it matches on the capability bit, not on a program name, so it reports an unusual privilege rather than a blacklist of software. Ordinary system daemons that legitimately hold these capabilities are excluded.

key.name: thermal-sense-enabled
key.summary: Retired: merged into the hwmon sense
key.description: The `thermal` sense was merged into `hwmon`, which reported the ACPI thermal-zone view. The kernel exposes the same sensors through both the thermal-zone and the hwmon trees and they agree, so one sense now reports chips, fans, liquid cooling and thermal zones together. This key is still honoured: setting it to true grants the `hwmon` sense, so a grant made before the merge is not revoked by it.

key.name: display-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read the screen's brightness and output state
key.description: When true, Chronoa may read display state from sysfs - backlight brightness, whether an output is connected, and the current mode. Off by default. This reads the panel's own backlight setting; it is not a light sensor and cannot tell you how bright the room is.

key.name: network-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read local network interface state
key.description: When true, Chronoa may read link state for each network interface - up or down, carrier present, negotiated speed - and the machine's configured DNS servers. Off by default. Interface state only: it does not read traffic contents, does not scan nearby networks, and does not perform any radiometric sensing.

key.name: bluetooth-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa list paired and nearby Bluetooth devices
key.description: When true, Chronoa may list the Bluetooth adapters on this machine and the device addresses and names it can see. Off by default. It reads the local controller's own registry; it does not track devices, does not record presence history, and cannot tell whether a device is in the room - Bluetooth range is far too coarse and the controller gives no ranging data.

key.name: camera-sense-enabled
key.summary: Retired: merged into the capture sense
key.description: The `camera` sense was merged into `capture`. They already shared the device-holder lookup - `camera` imported `contention.describe` - and `contention` already walked both the video and the sound nodes, so one sense now reports every capture device, what the kernel calls it, and whether anything holds it open. This key is still honoured: setting it to true grants the `capture` sense, so a grant made before the merge is not revoked by it.

key.name: rfsense-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa sample the WiFi link and notice movement
key.description: When true, Chronoa may sample each wireless interface's link quality from /proc/net/wireless and track how much the signal is varying, which is a real and long-established indication that something in the room is moving. Off by default. This is RSSI-only, which is the coarser half of radio sensing: it notices movement, not who or what, it gives no position, and it cannot distinguish a person from a pet, a curtain or a rotating fan. It reports the machine's sensing ceiling honestly rather than implying a capability it does not have. No frames, no image, no camera.

key.name: thermalgrid-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read a thermal camera array if one is attached
key.description: When true, Chronoa may probe the machine's I2C buses for a Melexis MLX90640 (32x24, 768 pixels) or Panasonic AMG8833 (8x8, 64 pixels) infrared array and, if one answers, report its temperature grid. Off by default. This is the real thermal-imaging path and it needs the sensor wired to I2C - no array, no grid, and this says so rather than substituting the CPU's own thermal zones, which measure the machine and not the room. A grid read here is coarse enough that it shows a warm shape, not a face.

key.name: hwmon-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read the machine's hardware monitoring sensors
key.description: When true, Chronoa may read the kernel's hwmon class - fan speeds in RPM, and the temperature, voltage, current and power readings each driver exposes, with each chip identified by its driver name. Off by default. Read-only, and it complements the thermal sense rather than repeating it: the thermal zones report the CPU and board, while hwmon is where fan RPM, SSD temperature, WiFi chip temperature and battery voltage live. Slots a driver declares but does not populate are reported as unpopulated rather than as a reading, because those slots read back as zero.

key.name: modelfit-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa check which language models this machine can actually run
key.description: When true, Chronoa may ask the local Ollama which models are installed, compare their on-disk size against this machine's available memory, and report whether the model currently configured is present and fits. Off by default. Read-only: it reports and recommends, and never downloads, loads, unloads or changes a model. This exists because the configured model is otherwise chosen by a two-way hardware tier that never checks what is installed or whether it fits - on a 31GB machine that still selects the same 2.5GB model it would choose on a 16GB one, and reports nothing if that model is not present at all.

key.name: mount-control-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa mount and unmount filesystems
key.description: When true, Chronoa may mount or unmount a filesystem through the desktop disk service, so that service's own authorisation rules apply. Off by default: mounting runs code from a device that was not there a moment ago, and unmounting something in use can lose work. Listing what is mounted needs no permission.

key.name: idle-timeout-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa change when the screen blanks
key.description: Off: Chronoa can report the current idle timeout and whether the screen locks, but cannot change either. It has its own key rather than sharing the lock skill's, because whether the machine locks itself is a standing policy decision rather than a one-off action.

key.name: appearance-control-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa change the desktop appearance
key.description: Off: Chronoa can report whether the desktop is set to a light or dark appearance but cannot change it. Restyling a desktop unasked, mid-document, is disruptive in a way that reading it is not.

key.name: timezone-control-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa change the system timezone
key.description: Off: Chronoa can report the current timezone and list the available ones but cannot change it. It is a system-wide change that moves every timestamp on the machine at once, and it needs root.

key.name: bluetooth-control-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa switch the Bluetooth adapter
key.description: Off: Chronoa can report which Bluetooth devices are paired and whether the adapter is on, but cannot turn it off. Separate from the bluetooth sense's own permission, because noticing a headset and being willing to have it disconnected mid-call are different agreements.

key.name: mic-control-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa mute the microphone
key.description: Off: Chronoa can report whether the microphone is muted but cannot change it. Output volume and mute are separate skills that need no such permission; this covers the input side, which is the more privacy-relevant of the two.

key.name: screen-lock-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa lock this session
key.description: Off: Chronoa cannot lock the screen. It has its own permission rather than sharing input control, because it does not act on the interface - it ends the current session's access to the machine, and a person mid-sentence loses the floor.

key.name: trash-empty-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa empty the trash
key.description: Off: Chronoa can list what is in the trash but cannot empty it. Not the same permission as deleting files - everything in the trash was already removed from where it was and is recoverable, and emptying it is the step that makes it unrecoverable.

key.name: service-control-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa change system services
key.description: When true, Chronoa may start, stop, restart, enable or disable a system service. Off by default: these are root-owned units, the wrong one can take down something another person is relying on, and stopping the wrong one on a remote machine can lock you out. Listing services and reading their logs need no permission.

key.name: bulk-edit-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa edit many files at once
key.description: When true, Chronoa may replace a string across every file matching a pattern. Off by default, and separate from writing one named file: a pattern that matches in forty files rewrites forty files, and that blast radius is not knowable in advance. Without this, find_and_replace still runs as a dry run and lists what it would change.

key.name: usb-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read the USB devices attached to this machine
key.description: Reads the USB bus for attached devices, with their class, vendor, product and negotiated link speed. On by default like the other bus and disk senses. Covers what is plugged into ports, which the PCI inventory does not.

key.name: coredumps-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa report programs that crashed
key.description: Reports recorded crashes from the last week, and states whether crash recording is even enabled - a machine that records nothing is not a machine where nothing crashed. On by default: it reads the local crash store and never leaves the machine.

key.name: firewall-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa report whether a firewall is actually enforcing
key.description: Checks ufw, firewalld and the nftables/iptables ruleset, distinguishing a firewall that is installed from one that is enforcing, and reporting UNKNOWN rather than "unprotected" when a tool needs root. On by default: it reads the local firewall configuration.

key.name: updates-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa check for waiting package updates
key.description: Reports how many updates are waiting, and how old the package database the comparison was made against is. On by default: it reads the local package database and never leaves the machine.

key.name: faults-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read recent system errors
key.description: Reports errors and warnings the system journal has recorded recently, and states how far back the journal reaches. On by default: an empty error list from a machine whose journal could not be read is the failure this is designed to avoid, so it needs to be running for that distinction to be available.

key.name: snapshots-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa list rollback points
key.description: Lists btrfs snapshots and which subvolume is currently booted, which is what makes a rollback possible. Read-only - it never creates or deletes one. On by default: it reads filesystem metadata only.

key.name: sessions-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa see who else is on this machine
key.description: Reports who is logged in and which processes run as root outside the init system's own service tree. Off by default, and the only machine-state sense that is: this reports other people's presence on the machine rather than the machine's own hardware, so it waits to be asked for.

key.name: resources-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa check for resources running out
key.description: Reports zombie processes that were never reaped, whether swap is in use, and how close the open file-descriptor limit is. On by default: none of these look like high usage, which is why nothing else notices them.

key.name: filesystems-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read what is mounted and how much room is left
key.description: Reads the mount table and each filesystem's space and remaining inodes. On by default: this is the machine's own state, like the disk and power senses, and a filesystem can have bytes free while being unable to create another file.

key.name: services-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa read which system services have failed
key.description: Reads systemd's own view of which units are in a failed state, with the last few log lines from each. On by default because only failures are reported, not the whole service list.

key.name: timebase-sense-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa check whether the system clock is trustworthy
key.description: Reads the time zone and whether the clock is synchronised to a network time source. On by default: every reminder and timer is downstream of it, and an unsynchronised clock is invisible otherwise.

key.name: file-delete-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa delete files
key.description: When true, Chronoa may permanently delete files and directories it is asked to remove. Off by default, and separate from the general file-access permission: reading a directory and removing what is in it are different risks. Delete is not reversible through Chronoa itself - the filesystem's trash is not used.

key.name: process-kill-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa stop processes
key.description: When true, Chronoa may send a stop or kill signal to a running process. Off by default. A wrong process id can take down unsaved work, and Chronoa cannot tell an unsaved document from a saved one.

key.name: window-close-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa close windows
key.description: When true, Chronoa may ask a window to close. Off by default: closing a window can discard unsaved work, and the request is a polite ask rather than something Chronoa can verify was safe.

key.name: wifi-connect-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa change WiFi connections
key.description: When true, Chronoa may join, leave or change the machine's WiFi network. Off by default: this changes what the machine can reach, and a network change made on a spoken or misread instruction is not obvious to undo by looking at the screen.

key.name: input-control-enabled
key.summary: Let Chronoa control the pointer and keyboard
key.description: When true, Chronoa may move the pointer, click, and type text as named actions. Off by default, and deliberately separate from the vision sense: seeing a screen and controlling it are different risks, and together they would let any prompt injection in a web page or a file reach the machine. Every action is logged to the per-user tool-call audit log.
